chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Moms Mabley, John Mason and Bojangles at the Tree of Hope
summary: She met comedians Moms Mabley and John Mason, and Bill Bojangles, who could run backwards as fast as others ran forwards.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I think Josephine was younger. During that time I met, in fact I played for Moms Mabley. Her name was Jackie Mabley then. And John Mason - oh, they were the most fabulous comedians. They were the same on the street. John Mason had a little baby just could barely talk. He'd stand on the street and everybody would be laughing. They'd go around the Tree of Hope and he had taught this kid every curse word in the book. If you walked up and said, 'Hello, how are you, little -' he'd call you rotten and then John Mason, his father, would break down and laugh. That was his kicks during the time he wasn't working, to teach his own son these words. The Tree of Hope, that's where most of the performers used to hang out. During that period I met also Bojangles.

The guys were so fascinated - in the band, you know, John Williams and the group that I worked with - so fascinated with him that they used to hang out where he was. He was a great pool player. He'd bet like $500 on a game. He was very good at it and most times he'd win and also he used to bet some of the guys on the street that he could run backwards as fast as anyone running forward. He'd win that. I saw him running backwards. That's the funniest thing I've ever seen in my life. He was really great at doing things like that.
That was part of his dancing ability, wasn't it, the fact that he could run backwards?
I don't know but he could really run fast backwards.
